content:
Yes, though it's sometimes a bit messy to make a CSLib mwe that will work fully in the web editor, you can at least include all the imports necessary.

This should be easier once the web editor adds support for third-party libraries.

On that note: @Kim Morrison Is there a way I can track progress on that effort or even help out?

I'm not super sure who to talk to about this.

It's not just a matter of giving CSLib equal billing with Mathlib in the project selection box in live.lean-lang.org; we'd probably want to make sure this is done extensibily (and so others running their own live.lean-lang.org instances could easily plug in other projects).

@Rob Simmons, @Joachim Breitner, do either of you know who is most actively thinking about project selection in live.lean-lang.org, and could comment on plans or receptivity to PRs?

Technically adding more dropdown configurations is straightforward — as a technical matter I could add CSLib Latest CSLib Stable to the drop-down today, but it requires relatively straightforward changes to the FRO's private infrastructure configuration so isn't publicly PR-able, and it would be less visible. I could also (additionally or alternatively) add CSLib to "Mathlib Stable" and "Latest Mathlib" configurations. General extensibility is trickier.
3 messages were moved here from #CSLib > Is this provable ? by Chris Henson.

I noticed today that live.lean-lang.org now includes a drop down for "Stable (Mathlib + CSLib)". Not sure who to thank, but it's much appreciated! If there's ever any maintenance issues, please do ping me.

Small snippet to play with-

import Cslib

#check Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM
#check Cslib.Automata.εNA

(control-clicking stuff tries to go to the mathlib docs and gets 404, but that's less important :sweat_smile:)
Please consider this “soft launched and not a permanent promise to support” for now, but please do experiment and see if there are issues! Thanks for noting the control-click issue @Snir Broshi
@Chris Henson could you change the name of this thread to "CSLib in Lean web editor"? The current title doesn't really make sense (edit: thanks!)
(also, would be cool to see web editor support for the combinatorial games repo as well!)
Yes, I definitely agree with Kim's above sentiment that it would be great to have this extensible to other notable projects downstream of Mathlib.

Snir Broshi said:

(control-clicking stuff tries to go to the mathlib docs and gets 404, but that's less important :sweat_smile:)

are there cslib docs published somewhere stable? since they include mathlib docs transitively, it seems like it woudn't be too problematic to link to them and make control-click links work

(The current status is that live supports the latest-including-rc and latest-stable releases of both mathlib and cslib, and I think we can continue doing that somewhat stably, though I don't anticipate growing that list soon)
Yes, our docs are hosted on this leanprover webpage: https://leanprover.github.io/cslib/docs
